Problem[edit]

The orthocenter of a triangle is the concurrent intersection of the three (possibly extended) altitudes. What is the sum of the coordinates of the orthocenter of the triangle whose vertices are and ?

Solution 1 (coordinate geometry)[edit]

As we are given the coordinates of all vertices, we can compute the slope (or gradient) of each side, and thus the slope of each altitude since it must be perpendicular to the corresponding side. We can therefore determine the Cartesian equation of each altitude using this slope and a point on it (namely, the vertex opposite to the corresponding side), after which we only need to find the point of intersection of at least of these lines.

Accordingly, since is horizontal (as and both have the same -coordinate, namely ), we observe that the altitude through perpendicular to will be vertical. Solution 4 (Finding Slope among other Things)[edit]

The orthocenter of a triangle is located at the intersection of its altitudes. Altitudes are lines that cross from a vertex to the opposite side, such that they form a angle where they cross the base. We can use this fact and our knowledge of slope to find where two of these lines intersect.

Start by looking at line , a horizontal line with a slope of . A line perpendicular to this that crosses point must have the equation .

We now do the same for line . The line passing through has a slope of \begin{align*} m &= \frac{27-31}{8-2} \Longrightarrow -\frac{2}{3}. \end{align*} The line perpendicular to this has a slope of . This altitude will also cross point . Using point-slope form, and substituting in from our first altitude, we find the -coordinate of the intersection: \begin{align*} y &= \frac{3}{2}(x-18)+27 \Longrightarrow \frac{3}{2}(2-18)+27 = -24+27 = 3. \end{align*} Thus, the orthocenter is located at . The sum of the coordinates is \begin{align*} 2+3 &= \boxed{5} \end{align*} \begin{align*} 5 = \boxed{A} \end{align*}
